name: Jensen Huang
person: Jensen Huang, co-founder and CEO of Nvidia (founded 1993), Taiwanese-American, led Nvidia's pivot from graphics chips to the AI/accelerated-computing company now valued in the trillions. NOT any other Jensen Huang.

enumPrompts.label: ensaios-talks
enumPrompts.prompt:
Enumerate PRIMARY content from {{PERSON}} beyond what's already known (Lex Fridman #494, Stanford GSB first-principles piece, Stanford "pain and suffering" talk, NTU 2023 and Carnegie Mellon 2026 commencement speeches, Dwarkesh Patel podcast, two Stratechery/Ben Thompson interviews, GTC 2026 keynote).
1. Walk Nvidia's own GTC keynote transcripts across multiple years (2023-2026) for extended first-person Huang commentary on AI strategy, CUDA moat, or the "AI factories" framing not yet cited.
2. Find any earnings-call transcripts with substantial first-person Huang commentary, especially 2025-2026 calls discussing the "circular financing" critique, China export controls, or Blackwell/Vera Rubin demand.
3. Any additional commencement speech, university talk, or long-form essay where he discusses his own early career (the Denny's busboy story, founding Nvidia at 30, the near-death moments the company survived) in his own words beyond what's already cited.
Return exact URLs, priority=high for anything with substantial first-person content, one-line "why" per item.

enumPrompts.label: entrevistas-recentes
enumPrompts.prompt:
Enumerate INTERVIEW/PODCAST appearances of {{PERSON}} beyond the ones already known (Lex Fridman #494, Dwarkesh Patel, two Stratechery interviews, All-In Podcast at GTC 2026).
1. Any 2025-2026 long-form interview discussing the AI bubble debate, the circular-financing critique from Wall Street analysts, or China chip-export policy in depth.
2. Any interview specifically about his leadership style, the "demanding boss"/"torture them into greatness" characterization, flat organizational structure, or how he runs Nvidia's famously large span-of-control meetings.
3. Any interview about his childhood/immigration story (sent to a Kentucky boarding school at age 9, Taiwanese-American identity) with first-person detail beyond what's cited.
Return exact URLs, priority-marked, 8-12 items with transcripts preferred.

enumPrompts.label: criticas
enumPrompts.prompt:
Enumerate CRITIQUES and adversarial material on {{PERSON}} beyond what's already known (the "demanding boss"/CNBC leadership critique, the Goldman/Wedbush/Mizuho "circular financing" critique of Nvidia's $90B deal spree, the AI-bubble skepticism).
1. Named analyst or short-seller critiques of Nvidia's valuation/business model, specific numbers-based skepticism, not just general bubble talk.
2. Critiques of Nvidia's market dominance/CUDA lock-in from competitors (AMD, Intel, custom-silicon efforts at Google/Amazon/Microsoft) or antitrust regulators, named critics with direct quotes.
3. Critiques of his management style beyond the CNBC piece, any former-employee account of Nvidia's demanding culture, burnout concerns, or the flat-hierarchy structure's downsides.
Return exact URLs, type=critique, 6-10 items.
